ITS CLOSING CAVEAT IS ANSWERED AND ITS CENTRAL CLAIM IS CONFIRMED, NOT OVERTURNED. That note ends "NOT VERIFIED BY EXECUTION HERE: the mechanism was read from the code rather than reproduced with a concurrent client... A reproduction would be two overlapping tool calls against one server asserting the failure disappears when they are sequenced." Both halves have now been run — `sequenced_the_same_pair_always_succeeds` and the two spawn-based arms measured here — and its diagnosis holds exactly: the hazard is ORDER, not visibility, and read-after-write was never the problem.

⭐ ITS OTHER PREDICTION ALSO CAME TRUE, twenty-two days later and at cost. It said "THE GENERAL FIX IS A DESCRIPTION, NOT A FEATURE" and warned that collapsing one pair would not close an open set. The instance fix was built, the description was not, and the same user hit the same class through a different pair — which is the whole of fact:the-parallel-batch-class-recurred-because-only-its-instance-was-fixed. This node was right and was under-acted-on, which is worth more than being right.

🛑 WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED: the reproduction stays deliberately short of asserting that a concurrent batch FAILS. That is a scheduler outcome and pinning it would flap. The arms COUNT the outcome instead and are ignored by default.
